narrative:
The model estimates you have a 16% chance of failing your final year. While this is not a high probability, it is enough for the school to require you to take remedial courses as a precaution.

The prediction that you are at risk of failing is driven mainly by three aspects of your situation. First, you have had no past class failures, which is exactly average for students who passed and strongly pushes the model toward expecting you to succeed. However, two other factors pull in the opposite direction and outweigh that positive signal. Your amount of free time after school is low compared with most students who passed. The model sees this limited free time as a warning sign that you may be overloaded or struggling to balance your commitments. In addition, although you have a clear desire to pursue higher education, the model notes that this ambition alone is not currently translating into the study habits needed to secure a passing grade.

Because the lack of past failures is not enough to offset the concerns around your free time and study patterns, the overall prediction leans toward failure. To improve, you should look at how you are using the little free time you have and whether you can turn your ambition for higher education into more consistent weekly study. Even small increases in focused study time could shift your outlook and help you avoid the need for remedial courses next year. (218 words)
